props.statement: In the hydrogenation of carbon monoxide the reaction conditions and the nature of the catalyst determine the nature of the end products.

props.name: design choice: methanol from CO2 and H2
props.statement: Catalysts are now available that make the synthesis from CO2 and H2 just as possible as from CO and H2; the former therefore offers some advantages and was chosen.

props.name: co2 less health hazard
props.statement: Working with CO2 is less hazardous to the workers' health than working with CO, but in practice (as at Sterlington) a mixture of CO and CO2 is always used, so precautions still need attention.

props.name: co2 route analogous conditions

evidence.locator: p. 9, Methanol uit CO2 en H2

props.statement: In the CO2 route the hydrocarbon gases are first converted with steam into CO2 (CO) and H2, from which methanol is made under reaction conditions and with a catalyst analogous to the synthesis of methanol from CO and H2.

props.name: co2 route less dme
props.note: the product compositions are cited from litt. 4 (Oppau) and litt. 8 (Sterlington)
props.statement: Oppau (from CO) delivered a crude product of 90 % methanol and 1-2 % dimethyl ether, Sterlington (from natural gas, largely via CO2) one of 65 % methanol and 0.1 % dimethyl ether; although Sterlington consumes more hydrogen per mol methanol (lost as water), its yield of almost worthless dimethyl ether is smaller.

props.name: co2 route less heat less methane
props.statement: The reaction of CO with H2 to methanol releases 21.6 kcal/mol CO, that of CO2 with H2 11.8 kcal/mol CO2; the smaller heat of reaction gives less chance of local overheating in the reactor and therefore less methane formation.

props.name: coke oven gas ratio
props.statement: Coke-oven gas, another source of synthesis gas, has an H2 : CO ratio of 1.25 : 1, so part of the CO must be removed by steam conversion.

props.note: cited from FIAT Final Report (litt. 4; 'rapport 888' on p. 7 in the page image, 'no. 888 (1946)' in the reference list)
props.statement: At Oppau methanol was made from CO and H2 over a Zn-Cr catalyst (oxides reduced in the reactor) at 150 ata and 300 °C with a synthesis gas of 2 mol H2 per mol CO, made from water gas by partial steam conversion over an Fe catalyst; CO2 was removed by pressure washing and sulfur compounds, which inactivate the catalyst, by active carbon.

props.name: plant capacity 700 kg h
props.statement: The plant is designed for 700 kg methanol per hour (1500 t/yr for Dutch demand plus about 490 kg/h for a formaldehyde plant).

props.name: reaction enthalpy
props.note: the value at 298 K is cited from Kirk-Othmer (litt. 7); the 573 K value is the report's own calculation
props.statement: The reaction enthalpy of CO2 + 3 H2 -> CH3OH + H2O is 11,830 cal/mol methanol at 298 K (Kirk-Othmer); integrating the heat-capacity change gives 15.281 kcal per mol at 573 K; with 23.3 kmol methanol per hour the heat released is 3.535 x 10^5 kcal/h.

props.name: reactor balance kmol
props.statement: Reactor material balance per hour: in 41.5 kmol N2, 466 kmol H2, 156 kmol CO2; out 41.5 kmol N2, 396 kmol H2, 132 kmol CO2, 23.3 kmol methanol and 23.3 kmol water.

props.name: reactor exit b
props.statement: With 15 % conversion the reactor exit stream B contains 13.0 % N2, 65.0 % CO2, 8.84 % H2, 0.1 % methane, 8.34 % methanol and 4.7 % water.

props.name: reactor temperatures
props.statement: In the heat balance the reaction gases leave the reactor at 300 °C; the synthesis gases enter the reactor at 270 °C; to exchange the remaining heat internally the synthesis gases must have a heat content corresponding (graph 3) to 240 °C.

props.name: recycle temperatures
props.note: cited from Ind. Eng. Chem. 40 (1948) 2230, M.I. Karstens, Synthetic methanol (litt. 8)
props.statement: At Sterlington the methanol is separated at 90 °C; the recycle gas is pumped by an isentropic compressor, so its temperature rises to 110 °C.

props.name: sterlington conditions
props.note: cited from Ind. Eng. Chem. 40 (1948) 2230, M.I. Karstens, Synthetic methanol (litt. 8)
props.statement: In the Sterlington process (methanol from CO2 and H2) the reactor pressure is 300 ata; the reaction temperature is 270-300 °C with a new catalyst and rises with time to 350 °C; methanol is separated with water at 90 °C and 300 ata, its partial pressure then being 2.5 ata, so the recycle gas contains less than 1 % methanol.

props.name: sterlington model more economic
props.statement: Since CO was lost at Oppau and the Netherlands has sufficient natural gas for hydrogen, synthesis on the Sterlington model will probably be more economic.
